title: Australia, Philippines sign major defence agreement | ABC News Top Stories
transcript:
Speaker 0: ABC News.
Speaker 0: Ted O'Connor with the top stories.
Speaker 0: Australia and The Philippines have signed a major defense cooperation agreement on the sidelines of the ASEAN Summit in Manila.
Speaker 0: The agreement expands military cooperation and information sharing as well as bolstering The Philippines, Navy, and Coast Guard. Comes as an informal defense block of four nations, Australia, The United States, The Philippines, and Japan,
Speaker 0: nicknamed the squad, looks to counter China's influence in the South China Sea.
Speaker 0: Meanwhile, prime minister Anthony Albanese says he'll use a meeting with his Vietnamese counterpart
Speaker 0: to raise the case of an Australian pro democracy activist currently imprisoned in his country. Hip Tran is being detained in Ho Chi Minh City after disappearing in Cambodia on September 18.
Speaker 0: His supporters believe he was abducted by Vietnamese authorities who have in turn accused him of trying to enter the country illegally.
Speaker 0: There's been a significant breakthrough in space technology as SpaceX rocket has managed to return to its launch pad in Texas in a world first.
Speaker 0: After orbiting Earth a dozen times, it came back and was secured to the launching pad by mechanical arms.
Speaker 0: It's the next step in Elon Musk's effort to develop a fully reusable rocket,
Speaker 0: which would dramatically reduce the cost of space missions.
Speaker 0: For more news at any time, you can follow the ABC top stories podcast.
